item.text: Day one spent $89.84 and recorded two entries, both from the drawing-and-eligibility post. That’s an early signal; I’ll give both posts another day before shifting budget.

After two days, the drawing-and-eligibility post has four attributed entries at $23.32 each; the gift post has two at $46.74 each. I’ve shifted more of the remaining budget toward the stronger post while keeping the gift test running. The combined lifetime caps remain $750.

The campaign has spent $279.39 and recorded 11 attributed entries. The drawing-and-eligibility post continues to deliver entries at roughly half the gift post’s cost, so I’m keeping the current budget split.
Halfway through, spend is $365.44 with 16 attributed entries. The drawing-and-eligibility post now has 12 entries at $18.45 each, so I’ve increased its share again for the remaining four days.

After five days, the campaign has 19 attributed entries on $456.59 spend. I’ve paused the gift post and moved its available budget to the drawing-and-eligibility post, which has consistently produced entries at a lower cost.
Six days in, spend is $553.73 with 24 attributed entries. The active post continues to produce entries at about $20 each, and the remaining budget is paced across December 1 and 2.

The final day starts with $647.48 spent and 29 attributed entries. I’ve adjusted today’s pacing to use the active ad group’s remaining allowance, with the lifetime cap and midnight Eastern end time still in place.
The eight-day flight has ended, and the campaign is paused. I’m allowing one hour for reporting to catch up before collecting the recap.
